question: Does the relative odd/even thermal shape and common-profile-coordinate failure persist when all periods are doubled?
primary_readout: Same-area finite common profile transport J_m(U)-r_E J_m(D), m=1..6, with complete paired-batch covariance and fitted r_A/r_E uncertainty; use quotient-free polynomial form if source area is weak.
additional_readouts: fixed-p A/E/C/W response and previously defined affine-E4 and free-common-secant scores
full-p and central thermal-window residual moments, keeping the two scopes separate
N100-to-N400 relative-shape change with independent source-block covariance; no imposed area power
sampling: Same seed and counter block across the three N400 shapes. Independent of the N100 seed/block. One correlated N400 dependency group; no adaptive sample extension in this run.
resource: Local Mac, three single-threaded engine processes. No new server or GPU rental.
geometry: Every N100 period entry is multiplied by two. Same tau and rational O; first Smith(2,200), second Smith(10,40) for every pair. This is a homothetic scale, not an N200 Gaussian-norm change.
boundary: A prospective scale follow-up to an exploratory N100 mechanism. Numerical outcomes are not presumed; a weak target does not establish recovery of a model. Full-p results do not by themselves identify a critical-window field. No old-test campaign is assigned.
